summary: Field-of-view detection with a line-of-sight check, so hiding behind a wall actually works.
overview: Detects targets within a range and a view angle, then raycasts to confirm nothing blocks the line — which is what makes cover meaningful. Genre-agnostic: a stealth game uses it directly, a racing AI ignores it entirely.
useCases: Guard detection in a stealth game.
An enemy noticing the player entering a room.
Any "can this see that" question with obstacles in between.

params.tuning: Assign a head or eye transform. Left at the object's origin, a guard sees from its feet and cover stops working properly.
The FULL angle, so 90 means 45 degrees either side.
What blocks sight. Forgetting to include walls is the reason guards see through them.
Zero scans every frame. For a dozen guards, a tenth of a second is invisible to the player and much cheaper.

gotchas.title: The occlusion ray goes to the target's origin
gotchas.body: A target whose pivot is at its feet can be "hidden" by a low wall its head is clearly above. Aim at a chest-height point if that matters.
